change: Removed 'abs' from secondary: torso is braced against the bench so abs are not meaningfully active stabilizers in this prone position. Expanded mid back secondary to include Upper Traps alongside Rhomboids and Lower Traps, as upper traps act as shoulder-girdle stabilizers during the raise. Primary Anterior Deltoids confirmed correct.

No substantive changes. Primary (Posterior Deltoid + Rhomboids/Upper Traps/Lower Traps) and secondary (Rotator Cuff) confirmed correct by EMG research showing rear delts, rhomboids, and trapezius as prime movers with rotator cuff (infraspinatus, teres minor) as secondary stabilizers.

Moved biceps from primary to secondary. EMG studies confirm that for an overhand (pronated) grip pull-up, the latissimus dorsi is the prime mover; biceps brachii assist in elbow flexion as a secondary mover. The overhand grip reduces biceps dominance compared to supinated (chin-up) grip. All other secondaries retained unchanged.

No changes. Primary Lats only with biceps and all other back/shoulder muscles as secondary is confirmed correct. Wide grip further reduces biceps involvement vs normal grip, making Lats the sole primary mover.

Moved mid back (Rhomboids, Lower Traps) from primary to secondary. This is the same movement as wide grip pull-up viewed from the front — the latissimus dorsi is the prime mover; rhomboids and lower traps are secondary stabilizers/scapular retractors. Also added forearms (Wrist Flexors) secondary consistent with the other pull-up variants.
